classification.difficultyReason: Development: the hardest demand is explaining how equally spaced five-year and one-year intervals distort rates of change, while distinguishing a legitimate restricted line scale from an inherently defective scale. Across a–f, students also diagnose unequal numerical intervals, missing scale numbers, unequal bar widths and ambiguous 3D pictographs. These are routine linked critiques using the supplied teaching; the number of parts does not determine the rating.

content.prompt: Describe the misleading or poor features of these graphs.

spec.description: Truncated line-graph axis20–26, source curve preserved including approximate unlabelled2009/2011 values. No exact production readings are asked.
spec.answerVisibility: student question graph; assessed defects intentionally retained

answer.short: The restricted 20–26 scale magnifies the variation. A nonzero line-graph baseline alone is not necessarily misleading.
answer.worked: The line rises from about 20 to 25.5 thousand tonnes. The restricted 20–26 scale magnifies this change, but a clearly labelled nonzero baseline is not inherently misleading for a line graph.

spec.description: Equal physical tick intervals carry0,10,20,40; heights at20,40 and midway20–40. Irregular numeric scale is intentional.
spec.answerVisibility: student question graph; assessed defects intentionally retained

answer.short: Equal vertical intervals represent unequal increases: 0, 10, 20, 40.
answer.worked: The gaps 0–10, 10–20 and 20–40 are drawn equally. Their numerical increases are 10, 10 and 20, so the scale is inconsistent.

spec.description: No numerical y-axis labels; A,D,E bars within X/Y sets; source relative heights1,2,1 and3,4,2.
spec.answerVisibility: student question graph; assessed defects intentionally retained

answer.short: The vertical axis has no numbers, so amounts cannot be read.
answer.worked: Horizontal gridlines have no numerical labels. The bar heights can be compared, but the vitamin amounts in milligrams cannot be read.

spec.description: Week2 bar twice Week1 width and twice height; retain misleading area increase.
spec.answerVisibility: student question graph; assessed defects intentionally retained

answer.short: Week 2 is twice as wide as Week 1, exaggerating its appearance.
answer.worked: Week 2 has twice the height and twice the width of Week 1. Its area is four times as large, exaggerating a twofold increase in cases.

spec.description: Two explicit pentagonal-prism milk-carton pictographs with equal front shoulder/roof heights and differing widths. Perspective retained; no exact production reading claimed. Back edges are occluded by the opaque cartons in the source.
spec.answerVisibility: student question graph; assessed defects intentionally retained
spec.visibilityMethod: Visible edge segments computed from explicit prism faces and oblique viewing direction; source pictograph omits hidden internal edges.
spec.sourceGeometryReview: Final-size carton fidelity and silhouette/roof ambiguity require independent review.

answer.short: The cartons have different widths, and their 3D roofs make the reading height unclear.
answer.worked: Factory B is represented by a wider carton despite the same displayed height. The three-dimensional roof also leaves the height used to read volume unclear.

spec.description: Equal horizontal spacing for2006,2011,2012 with fares1,2.5,3; irregular time intervals intentional.
spec.answerVisibility: student question graph; assessed defects intentionally retained

answer.short: Equal spaces represent five years, then one year, distorting the rate of increase.
answer.worked: The first horizontal gap is five years (2006–2011); the second is one year (2011–2012). Drawing them equally distorts the rate of change.
